answer: A beacon registry can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to stake a pigment-marked bond tied to a unique hardware key before it may list offers. Like a juniper cutting that only roots once, an identity only becomes active after a 7-day bonding delay and a small proof-of-work fee. An attacker cloning a thousand identities must pay a thousand bonds and wait a thousand delays, while honest agents pay once and keep trading; slashing the bond on proven fraud makes mass fakery unprofitable.
